title: "Agentic Workflow"
description: "A workflow in which a model dynamically chooses steps or tools to complete a task."
term: "Agentic Workflow"
letter: "A"
category: "AI Agents"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

An agentic workflow lets an AI system decide some of the steps needed to
complete a task, rather than following only a fixed sequence of operations.
It may choose a tool, inspect the result, and decide what to do next.

## Technical explanation

An agentic workflow is an orchestration pattern in which a model or agent
selects actions at runtime, often in a loop that observes tool results and
revises its next step. Workflows range from mostly fixed pipelines with a
few model decisions to open-ended systems with broader autonomy.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Dynamic decisions can handle varied requests that are difficult to encode
as a fixed pipeline. The trade-off is less predictable execution, so
engineers need limits, observable traces, permissions, and task-specific
evaluations.

## How it works

The workflow provides instructions, context, a set of allowed actions, and
stopping rules. The model selects a step; orchestration code validates and
executes it; the result is returned to the model for another decision. A
workflow ends on a success condition, a limit, an error, or a request for
human input.

## Practical example

A research assistant can search a set of approved sources, open relevant
pages, and summarize evidence. The system can restrict domains, cap tool
calls, and require citations in its final response.

## Common misconceptions

- An agentic workflow is not always better than a deterministic pipeline.
- A longer chain of model decisions can increase latency and failure
  opportunities.
- Human review and explicit limits remain useful even when a model appears
  capable.
